learningObjectives: Differentiate between the various Pega GenAI tools.
Generate a Case Type, including the Case Life Cycle and Data Model, by using Pega GenAI Autopilot.
Generate Personas by using Pega GenAI Autopilot.
Generate data records and populate data in forms by using Pega GenAI Autopilot.

elements.description: A suite of generative AI-powered features integrated across Pega Platform, available beginning with Pega Infinity '23. It helps developers, learners, and users build applications, enhance learning, improve operational efficiency, and stay aligned with best practices.

Blueprint is a separate SaaS application-design tool. A business description leads to proposals for workflow, data and Personas that the team reviews before implementation. A proposal is not proof of production readiness or a guaranteed delivery time.

Autopilot assists application authors with suggestions for workflow, data and Personas. The reviewed curriculum describes it as a design-time accelerator; speed improvements depend on the actual work and are not a measured guarantee for every project.
Lets you develop custom Pega GenAI-powered capabilities using the Pega GenAI gateway; an add-on compatible with Pega Platform, Customer Service, or Sales Automation.
Provides expert advice and feedback on END-USER tasks at application RUNTIME — ideal for task-specific guidance relevant to a Pega Case.

elements.text: The suite's introduction in Infinity '23 does not date every feature. Availability, configuration, licensing, and collaboration requirements vary by feature and release; check the target release's documentation.

bulletPoints: Design-time helpers: Blueprint (pre-build SaaS design) and Autopilot (in-platform App Studio acceleration).

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Generative AI — Run-Time Tools and Custom AI

elements.term: Pega GenAI Agent and Tool Rules
elements.description: Configured Agents support automated Case actions and runtime conversations. Tool Rules describe available actions and their constraints; permissions, review and configuration are still required.
Gives employees, agents, and sellers instant answers and real-time guidance via a conversation interface, combining Pega GenAI with the organization's own procedural documents and knowledge bases.

The reviewed topic describes Search Assistant as Community search backed by Knowledge Buddy. Its historical documentation-search example uses a trailing question mark for AI answers; that example does not establish the only supported trigger in every later interface.

elements.text: Think of Pega GenAI as a crew: Blueprint is the architect (designs before build), Autopilot is the master builder's assistant (helps at design time), Coach and Agents are the on-site supervisors (help at run time), and Knowledge Buddy/Search Assistant are the reference librarians (answer questions on demand).

bulletPoints: Run-time helpers: Coach (end-user task advice) and Agent/Tool Rules (automate + converse).
Knowledge Buddy uses organizational knowledge; Search Assistant points to Pega material. The trailing-question-mark documentation example is scoped to the reviewed topic.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Pega GenAI Autopilot at Design Time

elements.description: Autopilot delivers real-time, context-aware guidance and task prioritization during development. For a loan app, it suggests application components including Case Types, fields in the Data Model, and Personas — and developers can review and modify any recommendation before generating it.
When you create a Case Type, Autopilot suggests names, a workflow, data objects, and Personas — accelerating design-time setup with AI-generated proposals the architect reviews and accepts.
Review generated recommendations against the application requirements before accepting them. AI output can contain mistakes; the topic explicitly calls for review.

elements.text: Autopilot is a GPS co-pilot: it proposes a fast route (Case Types, fields, Personas, sample data), but you keep your hands on the wheel — reviewing and modifying every suggestion before committing.

bulletPoints: Historical note: the topic says Autopilot is inactive by default in Infinity '23 and '24. Check the target release and configuration rather than treating that as the default in every version.
Autopilot can generate sample records for a data object and auto-fill a running Case's form with sample data to ease testing.
Autopilot can generate a recommended Insight from a natural-language prompt for analyzing application data.

elements.term: Blueprint as a SaaS design tool
elements.description: Blueprint operates independently of a Pega Platform instance and supplements the studios. Do not confuse independence from a Platform instance with unrestricted anonymous access: follow the current Blueprint account, invitation and collaboration requirements.

From a business-terms description, Blueprint proposes Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas, plus best-practice application templates, enabling quick design edits to fit requirements.

elements.text: Blueprint proposes a design that the team can refine and import as a starting point. Imported assets still need review, configuration and testing.

bulletPoints: Blueprint augments — it does NOT replace — App Studio and other Pega tools.
Pega GenAI PremBridge is NOT required to import Pega Blueprints into a new or existing application.
You create a Blueprint at pega.com/blueprint.

elements.description: A Step (available since Pega Infinity '24) that calls a configured GenAI Connect Rule from App Studio to send a prompt to an LLM and receive a response in one of three structures.
GenAI response types and their Data Model mapping:
items: Structured-Single: one object mapped to a Data Model field
Structured-List: multiple objects mapped to a page list
Unstructured: raw text mapped to a Text (paragraph) field

elements.description: You must identify a target field to write the response into, and add that target field to the application UI so the response can be displayed to the user.

elements.text: A Connect Step is like sending a structured form letter to an AI clerk: your Prompt is the request, you specify how the reply should be shaped (single, list, or freeform), and you reserve a mailbox (target field) on the UI to receive it.

bulletPoints: Connect Rules can mask sensitive data during the request/response cycle and change the response language based on the user's locale.
Example uses: summarize a complex Case for a CSR, or list documents a customer must submit.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Pega GenAI Agent and Tool Rules

elements.description: Configurable AI assistants that automate Case processing and provide run-time guidance. Governed by Tool Rules, they can run automations, start Cases, call other agents, and converse with users.

Detailed tool descriptions and constraints help guide agent actions. Runtime conversations can include extraction from uploaded documents. These features support the workflow but do not guarantee correct responses or replace access controls.

elements.text: An Agent is a capable digital teammate; Tool Rules are its job description and rulebook — defining exactly what it may do and the guardrails it must respect.

bulletPoints: Configured agents can reduce repetitive work and support runtime conversations.
Validate permitted actions, responses and data handling; governance features are not an automatic compliance certification.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Generate and review a Case Type

elements.description: In App Studio, start Case Type creation. Autopilot proposes names from the application name and metadata; choose a proposal or enter your own name.

Select Use Autopilot to suggest a Life Cycle and Data Model. Review and edit the proposed Stages and Steps, then click Next to review fields. Each field has a Name, Type and technical ID; edit, add or remove fields as needed.

After reviewing the proposals, Submit creates the Case Type. Inspect Workflow and Data model. Embedded Data and Data reference proposals can also create associated data objects; review those relationships.
The Persona topic uses Users > User management in App Studio. Autopilot proposes names and descriptions from application metadata. Choose a suggestion or enter a custom Persona name.
After creating the Persona, add it in Personas & Channels in the Case Life Cycle. This models user roles in the workflow; it is not proof that a specific account has all required runtime permissions.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Generate sample records and fill forms

elements.description: Select a data object and its Records tab, then Generate sample records with Autopilot. Review the requested record count and the generated field values. These samples can support testing before an external source integration exists.

While testing a Case, Fill form with AI populates the form fields. Those values become part of the Case data used by the application. Inspect them before continuing; filling a form is different from generating data-object records.

examPitfalls.title: Design-time vs. run-time tools
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The exam tests whether a tool acts at design time or run time. Blueprint and Autopilot are DESIGN-time; Coach and Agents are RUN-time.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Map each tool to its phase: Blueprint/Autopilot = build the app; Coach/Agents = help users while the app runs.

examPitfalls.title: Historical default versus current configuration
examPitfalls.trapDescription: In Pega Infinity '23 and '24, Autopilot features are OFF by default and need configuration to enable.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For a question explicitly about Infinity 23/24, use that historical note. Diagnose a current environment using its release-specific configuration and access requirements.

examPitfalls.title: Always review AI suggestions
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Accepting proposed workflow or field values without checking the business requirements.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Human-in-the-loop: review and modify recommendations (Case Types, fields, Personas, data) before generating.

examPitfalls.title: Coach vs. Knowledge Buddy
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Coach gives task-specific advice on a Case at run time; Knowledge Buddy answers questions from the org's procedural docs/knowledge bases.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Task advice on a specific Case → Coach. Conversational answers from knowledge bases → Knowledge Buddy.

examPitfalls.title: Blueprint independence and import
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Equating independence from a Platform instance with anonymous access, or treating import as production readiness.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Check the current Blueprint collaboration requirements. Blueprint supplements application development; PremBridge is not the import requirement described by the source.

examPitfalls.title: Connect Step response structures
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Choosing a response destination without first identifying the configured response structure.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: For the described Unstructured response, Text (paragraph) is the recommendation. Single and List map structured values; select a target and display it in a View when users need to see it.

examPitfalls.title: What Autopilot can generate
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Autopilot generates Case Types (with Life Cycle and Data Model), Personas, sample data records, form fill, and Insights — not production integrations or security.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Tie Autopilot to design-time generation of workflow, data, Personas, and sample data.

examPitfalls.title: Agent capabilities
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Agents can run automations, start Cases, call other agents, launch user actions, and extract data from uploaded documents — governed by Tool Rules.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Agent = action + conversation; Tool Rules = guardrails/governance.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer wants real-time, context-aware suggestions for Case Types, Data Model fields, and Personas WHILE building an application in App Studio. Which Pega GenAI capability is this?
practiceQuiz.hint: This GenAI feature accelerates application design inside App Studio at design time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Autopilot provides the application-authoring suggestions described in this topic. Coach supports runtime tasks, Knowledge Buddy uses knowledge sources and Search Assistant supports finding Pega material.

optionExplanations.A: Autopilot assists the author during application design.
optionExplanations.B: Coach advises users performing tasks in a running application.
optionExplanations.C: Knowledge Buddy answers questions from organizational knowledge.
optionExplanations.D: Search Assistant finds relevant Pega Community material.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A CSR at RUNTIME needs expert, task-specific advice on how to handle the current complaint Case. Which tool is designed for this?
practiceQuiz.hint: Run-time advice on end-user tasks for a Case.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Coach provides runtime advice for end-user tasks. Blueprint and the described Autopilot authoring features support development; documentation search is separate from Case coaching.

optionExplanations.A: Coach's runtime task guidance fits the current complaint.
optionExplanations.B: Autopilot helps authors design rather than advise this CSR task.
optionExplanations.C: Blueprint designs applications rather than guide an active complaint.
optionExplanations.D: Documentation search is not an in-case coaching capability.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO Pega GenAI tools operate at DESIGN time to help build an application?
practiceQuiz.hint: Designing the app vs. helping users at run time.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint (pre-build SaaS design) and Autopilot (App Studio acceleration) are design-time GenAI tools. Coach (end-user task guidance) and Agents (automated Case processing) operate at run time. No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: Blueprint supports application design before the build.
optionExplanations.B: Autopilot helps authors configure the application.
optionExplanations.C: Coach advises end users at runtime.
optionExplanations.D: Agents execute configured actions for runtime users.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A team complains that Autopilot suggestions never appear in their Pega Infinity '24 environment. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: Autopilot features are inactive by default and require additional configuration to enable
Autopilot only works in Dev Studio
Autopilot requires PremBridge to design Case Types

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about whether Autopilot features are on or off by default in Pega Infinity '23/'24.
practiceQuiz.rationale: In Pega Infinity '23 and '24, Autopilot features are inactive by default and must be explicitly configured and enabled before use. The other statements misrepresent Autopilot's availability and scope.

optionExplanations.A: The question's specified releases require enabling these features.
optionExplanations.B: App Studio supports the Autopilot features in this scenario.
optionExplanations.C: The stated release includes them rather than removing them.
optionExplanations.D: PremBridge is not the activation requirement described here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Autopilot proposes a Case Type workflow and a picklist's choices. What should the developer do before generating them?

options.text: Review and modify recommendations to fit the application requirements before accepting them
Submit them to the LSA for compilation

practiceQuiz.hint: Autopilot requires a human to review suggestions before the system generates or acts on them.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source requires review of Autopilot suggestions. Verify the workflow and field proposals rather than accepting generated content blindly.

optionExplanations.A: Review ensures generated suggestions fit the actual requirements.
optionExplanations.B: Unreviewed generation can preserve errors or irrelevant assumptions.
optionExplanations.C: Suggestions do not require an LSA compilation step.
optionExplanations.D: Exporting to Blueprint is not the required review procedure.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is demoing Pega Blueprint to a business stakeholder who has provided a business-terms description of a new application. Which THREE items can Blueprint automatically propose from that description?

options.text: Case Types and Case Life Cycles

practiceQuiz.hint: Blueprint proposes the application skeleton — Case Types, Life Cycles, Data Models — but not server infrastructure.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint proposes Case Types, Case Life Cycles, Data Models, data objects, and Personas based on a business description. It does not provision hardware or server infrastructure. No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: The workflow proposal includes cases and their lifecycles.
optionExplanations.B: Data proposals help describe the application's business information.
optionExplanations.C: Persona proposals identify the intended users.
optionExplanations.D: A design proposal does not provision production hardware.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A solutions consultant is introducing Pega Blueprint to a client audience that has never used the tool before. Which statement correctly describes Pega Blueprint?

options.text: It is a separate SaaS design tool that supplements Pega studios; use its current account and collaboration requirements
It fully replaces App Studio and Dev Studio
It can only be used by Lead System Architects
It requires PremBridge to import its output into Pega

practiceQuiz.hint: Separate design tooling does not replace implementation or eliminate access requirements.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Blueprint operates separately from the Platform instance and supplements application design. Check its current collaboration requirements; independence is not a guarantee of anonymous access.

optionExplanations.A: Blueprint is separate from the runtime instance and supplements the studios.
optionExplanations.B: Generated designs still need application implementation and configuration.
optionExplanations.C: Collaboration is not restricted to Lead System Architects.
optionExplanations.D: PremBridge is not required for Blueprint import.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Connect Generative AI Step is configured with the Unstructured response type and returns long JSON text. Which field type does the reviewed topic recommend as its destination?
practiceQuiz.hint: Think about which response structure handles free-form, unstructured text output from an LLM.
practiceQuiz.rationale: For this explicitly Unstructured response, the source recommends Text (paragraph). JSON text alone does not establish that every Connect response should be treated as unstructured.

optionExplanations.A: Paragraph text fits the unstructured response described in the scenario.
optionExplanations.B: Currency cannot represent the long mixed-content response.
optionExplanations.C: A Boolean can only represent a true-or-false value.
optionExplanations.D: A date field cannot store the described response content.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO are valid response structures for a Pega GenAI Connect Step?

options.text: Structured - Single (a field/value or short page, auto-mapped to a Data Model field)
Structured - List (a list of fields/values mapped to an embedded data list)

practiceQuiz.hint: Single, List, and Unstructured are the three structures.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The three valid response structures for a Connect Generative AI Step are Structured-Single, Structured-List, and Unstructured. The other two options are invented distractors. No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: Single responses map one structured result.
optionExplanations.B: List responses map repeated structured results.
optionExplanations.C: Encrypted-Binary is not one of the stated response structures.
optionExplanations.D: Compiled-Java is not a GenAI Connect response structure.

practiceQuiz.scenario: After configuring a Connect Step's Prompt and response mapping, what additional step is required so the user can SEE the response?

options.text: Identify a target field and add it to the application's UI

practiceQuiz.hint: Where does the response get written and shown?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Identify the response target field and add it to a View when users must see the response. Mapping a value and displaying it are separate configuration steps.

optionExplanations.A: A displayed target field makes the returned information visible.
optionExplanations.B: Ruleset locking does not add the response to a view.
optionExplanations.C: A role grants permissions rather than display returned data.
optionExplanations.D: RPA configuration is unrelated to displaying this response.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An employee needs instant, conversational answers drawn from the company's own procedural documents and knowledge bases. Which tool fits?
practiceQuiz.hint: Knowledge Buddy combines organizational knowledge bases with conversational AI for instant answers.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Knowledge Buddy combines Pega GenAI with the organization's procedural documents and knowledge bases to deliver instant, contextual conversational answers. Coach advises on specific Case tasks; Autopilot and Blueprint are design-time tools.

optionExplanations.A: Knowledge Buddy answers using the organization's knowledge sources.
optionExplanations.B: Coach targets advice for a specific ongoing task.
optionExplanations.C: Autopilot targets application authors at design time.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO capabilities are provided by Pega GenAI Agents (with Tool Rules)?

options.text: Run an automation, start a Case, call another agent, or launch a user action
Process and extract data from uploaded documents during a conversation
Replace the need for any security or compliance controls

practiceQuiz.hint: Actions + document extraction; Tool Rules add governance.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Agents can run automations, start Cases, call other agents, launch user actions, and extract data from uploaded documents. Tool Rules ADD governance/security (they don't remove it), and agents don't compile Java. No partial credit.

optionExplanations.A: Configured tools let an agent perform permitted actions.
optionExplanations.B: Document processing can supply information during a conversation.
optionExplanations.C: Automated actions still require authorization and governance controls.
optionExplanations.D: Java compilation is not the conversational capability described here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In the documentation-search example described by the reviewed Generative AI topic, what query suffix is used to ask for an AI answer?

options.text: Add a question mark to the end of the search query

practiceQuiz.hint: A specific punctuation character at the end of a search query triggers OpenAI-powered search.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The reviewed example uses a trailing question mark. This is scoped to that described interface, not a claim that every later search tool supports only this trigger.

optionExplanations.A: The cited documentation curriculum uses a trailing question mark.
optionExplanations.B: This prefix is not the invocation described in the source.
optionExplanations.C: PremBridge concerns GenAI connectivity rather than search syntax.
optionExplanations.D: Prediction Studio is not the documentation site's search interface.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which Pega GenAI tool lets you develop CUSTOM GenAI-powered capabilities using the Pega GenAI gateway as an add-on?
practiceQuiz.hint: Pega GenAI Connect is the add-on gateway for building custom GenAI capabilities in Pega applications.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The reviewed topic identifies GenAI Connect as an add-on for custom capabilities through the GenAI gateway. Check actual licensing and deployment requirements for the chosen feature.

optionExplanations.A: Connect is the custom-capability gateway option described here.
optionExplanations.B: Coach offers task guidance rather than this custom integration route.
optionExplanations.C: Search Assistant retrieves Pega material rather than build custom capabilities.
optionExplanations.D: Blueprint proposes application designs rather than this gateway integration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Beginning with which Pega Infinity release did the Pega GenAI suite of features become available?
practiceQuiz.hint: The Pega GenAI feature set first became available starting with a specific Pega Infinity release.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Pega GenAI suite began with Pega Infinity '23. This is not a claim that every current feature existed in that release: for example, the App Studio Connect Generative AI Step is described for Infinity '24. Check feature availability for the target release.

optionExplanations.A: The suite began in this release; individual features have different introductions.
optionExplanations.B: This predates the suite introduction stated in the curriculum.
optionExplanations.C: This version predates the described GenAI suite.
optionExplanations.D: The suite existed before this later release.

practiceQuiz.scenario: During development a BA wants Autopilot to make testing easier by populating realistic values. Which Autopilot capabilities support this?

options.text: Generate sample records for a data object and auto-fill a running Case's form with sample data

practiceQuiz.hint: Autopilot can generate sample data records and auto-fill a running Case's form fields for testing.
practiceQuiz.rationale: These are two documented testing aids: generate data-object sample records and fill a Case form. Form values become Case data; they still need review before continuing the test.

optionExplanations.A: Sample records and form values support development-time testing.
optionExplanations.B: Generating samples does not provision production infrastructure.
optionExplanations.C: Relevant-record marking controls reuse rather than data generation.
optionExplanations.D: Locking a ruleset prevents edits rather than populate test values.

quickRecap.value: Suite of generative AI features across Pega Platform since Pega Infinity '23.
Blueprint (SaaS pre-build design) and Autopilot (App Studio acceleration: Case Types, Data Model, Personas, sample data, Insights).
Coach (end-user task advice on a Case) and Agent/Tool Rules (automate Case processing + conversational support with guardrails).
Knowledge Buddy uses organizational sources; Search Assistant supports Pega material discovery. Search behavior is interface/version specific.
Historical Infinity 23/24 default note; check the target version and always review generated proposals.
Separate SaaS design tool with current access requirements; supplements the studios and proposes assets for implementation.
Define a Prompt; responses: Structured-Single, Structured-List, Unstructured (→ Text paragraph). Set a target field and add it to the UI; can mask data + localize.
Configured actions and document extraction support runtime tasks; verify permissions, responses and controls.
Review names, lifecycle and fields before Submit; Persona suggestions can be added to Personas & Channels.
Generate sample data-object records or Fill form with AI; filled values become Case data.
